messages:
Ana: Heads up — finance just flagged our committed spend in eu-west4. They want us to evaluate moving part of the GPU commitments to us-west1 where hourly committed rates look better. Any red flags?

Alex: Do we have concrete per-region numbers yet or is this exploratory?

Ana: Exploratory but I pulled quick cost deltas from the billing export. Rough snapshot:
- us-west1 (p4d-equivalent): $3.40/hr committed vs on-demand $4.20/hr
- eu-west4 (p4d-equivalent): $4.75/hr committed vs on-demand $5.60/hr
Also noticed egress premium EU->US ~ $0.09/GB which could eat savings if we shift too much traffic.

Maya: +1 to be careful. Our EU customers (auth/data residency) are ~62% of inference qps during business hours. Latency adds matter. We saw median p95 go from 110ms -> 160ms when routing EU traffic to us-west1 in the last DR test.

Jamal: Two thoughts:
1) We should model net savings after egress and extra cross-region replication cost, not just raw committed GPU delta.
2) Consider mixing: keep a smaller EU reserved pool for latency/DR and shift non-latency-sensitive slices (batch embeddings, nightly re-embedding jobs) to us-west1.

Todd: Also confirm region availability — some GPU SKUs are flaky in eu-west4 for the next 90 days (quota backlogs). If we reduce EU commit too aggressively we might not be able to re-up quickly.

Alex: I can run a quick cost model + capacity probe. Will need two inputs: current qps by route (by region + latency-class) and 30/60/90 day forecast. Ana can you share the finance CSV?

Ana: Dropping the billing export query I ran (BigQuery):
```sql
SELECT region, sku, SUM(cost) as cost, SUM(usage_amount) as hours
FROM `redwood-billing.data.gcp_billing_export`
WHERE sku_description LIKE '%NVIDIA%'
  AND usage_start_time BETWEEN '2025-11-01' AND '2026-01-31'
GROUP BY region, sku
ORDER BY cost DESC
LIMIT 20;
```
Results are attached in the spreadsheet I just shared — link in #eng-finance.

billing-bot: Alert: Detected spike in inter-region egress on 2026-01-12 03:14 UTC — 5.2TB (label: nightly-backup).

Alex: Good catch — that backup ran to us-west1 for warm standby and explains one-time egress. If that pattern repeats monthly it changes the math.

Maya: For regulatory customers we should likely keep full EU-reserved capacity. For the rest: Jamal's idea of partitioning workloads is best. Also we need a SLO review before we move production traffic across regions.

Jamal: We can implement a placement policy:
- Latency-critical routes: prefer same-region reserved capacity (EU, US) with failover to other region only in degradation.
- Batch and background: route to lowest-cost region (us-west1) and use preemptible/spot where possible.
- Maintain min 20% reserved in EU as a buffer for spikes.

Todd: Ops questions: how long to move commit windows? If we reduce EU commit we need to align with provider contract cycles (30/60/365). Also check early-termination penalties for some committed SKU types.

Ana: Finance says we have a quarterly commit window for most committed GPUs. Next window is in 6 weeks. They want recommendations by EOW.

Alex: I'll run two things today: capacity availability probe and a net-savings model (takes egress + replication + preemption risk into account). ETA end of day.

Maya: I'll pull customer traffic split and latency-sensitive route list. Jamal/Todd can we get a small playbook for partitioning (routing rules + rollout plan)?

Jamal: I can draft the routing snippets. Example rule in our placement config: 
```yaml
placement_rules:
  - route: /api/v1/embed/batch
    prefer_regions: [us-west1, us-central1]
    reserved_required: false
    allow_preemptible: true
  - route: /chat/v1
    prefer_regions: [eu-west4]
    reserved_required: true
    failover: [us-west1]
```
Will share PR for the config and the rollout runbook.

Alex: FYI running the capacity probe now, will post raw results. If anyone sees odd quota numbers poke @cloud-ops.

Ana: Thanks all. Primary asks: (1) Alex — cost model + probe EOD, (2) Maya — definitive customer-latency map, (3) Jamal/Todd — draft placement + rollout by Wed. Finance needs recommendation before the commit window.

Maya: noted.

Jamal: noted.

Todd: noted.

Ana: :thumbsup:
